items.name: rule1
items.text: A board nailed to a post, the paint run in the damp. A hand with one finger across its lips, and under it in careful capitals: RULE ONE. WALK SOFT.
items.line: {worried}Walk soft. I'm walking soft. Am I walking soft? You're walking soft. I think we're both walking soft.

items.name: thorn
items.text: A thorn bush hung with strips of cloth, dozens, red and ochre and blue and grey. Each is knotted tight. Somebody tied each one on and whispered into it first.
items.line: {awed}You whisper a wish and tie it on. Ma did it every year. ...I never found out what she asked for.

items.name: jar
items.text: A jar on a hook, full of a green glow. Not a flame: a fungus, kept alive in a little damp moss, so the light never flickers and never smells of smoke. Smoke carries.
items.line: {thinking}That's clever. ...Is that clever? It's very clever.

items.name: stump
items.text: A great old stump with a round door and one small lit window. A tin chimney the width of a thumb. Nothing is smoking. Somebody very small is trying to look like nobody's home.
items.line: {sly}Hello? ...Sorry. Sorry, we're leaving.

items.name: shoes
items.text: A rail with three pairs of shoes hung out to dry, all soled in thick grey felt. You hold one up to your ear and listen to nothing. It's the quietest shoe you've ever heard.
items.line: {sheepish}I can hear my own ear.

items.name: rule2
items.text: RULE TWO. NO SINGING. And under it, smaller, in a different chalk: (HUMMING COUNTS.)
items.line: {sheepish}...I hum when I'm scared. I'm humming now. Am I? Oh no.

items.name: giant
items.text: A trunk as long as a barn and as wide as a door, felled so long ago it's turned into a hill. Moss, shelf fungus, one small mushroom wearing a bigger one as a hat. The broken end is wide enough to crawl into, and somebody has, and left.
items.line: {awed}It's got a hole you could live in. Somebody did. Look, there's a spoon.

items.name: shrine
items.text: A little stack of stones with a nook in it: a candle stub wrapped in felt and a pinch of dried flowers. The woodcutters didn't sing to the trees. They left a candle and kept quiet.
items.line: {worried}A candle. For who? ...For it?

items.name: axe
items.text: An axe sunk in a stump, the handle wrapped in rag so it won't clack when it's pulled out. It's still stuck. Whoever wrapped it never came back to pull.
items.line: {scared}Don't pull it. Don't. ...Was I going to? No.

items.name: boot
items.text: One felt-soled boot lying on its side, not worn through. Not a boot you'd leave. Somebody was moving fast and quiet at once, which is very hard to do.
items.line: {scared}Where's the other one?

items.name: thorn
items.text: A thorn tree at the oak's foot, hung with cloth strips, the oldest gone grey as ash. At the bottom is a new one: a scrap of blue scarf, the knot tied by small, careful hands.
items.line: {sad}That one's mine. ...I wished for something. It's rude to say.

items.name: mouse
items.text: A stump with a door painted on it, and a mouse in a thimble for a helmet who looks at you, looks at your boots, and goes in. The door shuts without a sound.
items.line: {glee}A guard mouse! Hello, sir! We're friends, sir!

items.name: jar
items.text: A jar of glow on a post, hung low, at child height. Somebody didn't want a little one to trip.
items.line: {proud}That's how you do it. ...I'd have put it higher. No. Lower. Fine.

items.name: nest
items.text: A nest on the ground, empty. The shells have been folded in neatly and tucked beside it. Neat birds.
items.line: {thinking}Do birds tidy? ...Do I tidy? Don't answer that.

items.name: moss
items.text: Moss thick enough to sleep on. You press it. It presses back, softly, and forgives you.
items.line: {grin}I'm going to sleep here. No. Not here. Somewhere with a roof.

items.name: bell
items.text: A small brass bell on a post, wrapped in felt and tied with string. A children's bell: the little ones used to ring it to say they were home. Then somebody wrapped it, and nobody unwrapped it.
items.line: {sad}...I used to ring that. It went ding like a spoon on a cup.

items.name: shoes
items.text: Little felt shoes in a row, from toddler to nearly grown. Each pair has a name chalked on the sole: PIP, DOT, WREN. The last pair is blank.
items.line: {sad}Mine were over there. ...They were over there.

items.name: rule0
items.text: A board with a rule, and under it, in wobbly chalk: RULE ZERO. HOLD HANDS. Somebody has added: (EVEN IF YOUR HANDS ARE STICKY.)
items.line: {grin}That's Wren. Wren's rules are the best rules.

items.name: hoop
items.text: A hoop and a stick, left where the game stopped. There's a footprint in the mud inside the hoop, a small one, pointing home.
items.line: {worried}It's pointing home. Good. That's good.

items.name: mice
items.text: A mouse house under a root. Someone has built it a twig fence and left a toast crumb at the door. A note: PLEASE BE QUIET (MICE).
items.line: {glee}They're very quiet already!

items.name: rule4
items.text: RULE FOUR. IF IT LISTENS, STAND STILL. Somebody has gone over the word STILL, three times, in thicker paint.
items.line: {scared}Stand still. Good. I can do still. I'm so good at still.

items.name: thorn
items.text: A thorn bush on the lean, hung so heavy with cloth strips that it droops. They're all the same grey now. The wishes have worn the colour out of them.
items.line: {sad}That's a lot of wishes. ...Do you think any of them came true?

items.name: shrine
items.text: A shrine stuffed in the crook of a leaning trunk: a felted candle stub, a button, a thimble, a pressed leaf. Small offerings. Nothing a hungry thing would want.
items.line: {thinking}That's the point, isn't it. Nothing to want.

items.name: jar
items.text: A jar of glow on a post. The pines lean away from it, or toward it. It's hard to tell, with pines.
items.line: {awed}They're leaning at it like they're reading over its shoulder.

items.name: cairn
items.text: A cairn of seven stones, one for each person who got through this stretch. The eighth stone, on top, has been turned face down. Out of respect, probably.
items.line: {sad}Seven. ...That's not very many.

items.name: rule3
items.text: RULE THREE. NO AXES AFTER DUSK. A second line, newer: NO AXES AT ALL. A third, in a hurry: PLEASE.
items.line: {worried}Three rules. They were running out of rules, Sword. Or running out of patience.

items.name: shoes
items.text: A rack of felt shoes beside the treadle path, so you could change before the planks. The planks creak. The shoes are why they didn't.
items.line: {proud}Soft shoes for hard planks. Ma would've made us wear them.

items.name: jar
items.text: A jar of glow set where the path goes dark, so you can find the next plank. The moss in it glows without being asked.
items.line: {thinking}It's moss. It just does it. I like that.

items.name: stump
items.text: A stump with a small door and a doormat the size of a stamp: WELCOME (QUIETLY).
items.line: {sly}We'll be so quiet.

items.name: bell
items.text: A bell on the gorge's lip, wrapped in felt and wound round with rope. This is the bell that used to ring the hours across the drop. Nothing rings now. The wood has been counting without it.
items.line: {worried}They tied up the bell. So it wouldn't tell it where they were.

items.name: thorn
items.text: A thorn tree leaning out over the gorge, hung with cloth strips. They flick in the updraught without a sound. Every one is tied facing the drop.
items.line: {awed}They're wishing at the bottom. Why would you wish at the bottom?

items.name: giant
items.text: A trunk laid across the gorge's near lip, as a bridge once and a bench now. The moss is worn off the middle where people sat to look.
items.line: {grin}Sit on it. Go on. It's the best view in the wood.

items.name: cairn
items.text: A cairn on the ledge, and a hat balanced on top, brim down. It's held there with a stone. It's been held there a long time.
items.line: {sad}Somebody's hat. ...Somebody made sure it stayed.

items.name: shoes
items.text: A rack of shoes with felt tied round every sole, and a second rack of saw teeth with felt tied round every tooth. The woodcutters worked in a hush. You can see the effort.
items.line: {awed}Even the saw had socks.

items.name: rule3b
items.text: RULE THREE AND A HALF. CUT SLOW. A third of the planks stacked here are stamped SLOW in black. They're perfectly square.
items.line: {proud}Slow is good. Ma says fast is for people who like splinters.

items.name: shrine
items.text: A shrine at the end of the sawpit with a felted candle and a tiny saw carved from a twig. An offering to the saw, so it wouldn't squeak.
items.line: {sly}It's working. The saw hasn't said a word.

items.name: cap
items.text: A cap left on a stump, a pencil behind its band. A tally of planks on the stump top, in neat fives. The last five has only four.
items.line: {worried}They stopped at four. Why would you stop at four?

items.name: rule5
items.text: RULE FIVE. IF IT STOPS, YOU STOP. Underneath, tallied in scratches: forty-one marks. The last twelve are very close together.
items.line: {scared}...Forty-one times. Somebody stopped forty-one times.

items.name: shrine
items.text: A shrine in the notch of an old stump: a candle, a button, a child's tooth, a note: FOR LUCK. KEEP.
items.line: {sad}I'm not going to take the tooth.

items.name: mouse
items.text: A mouse's door under the fox's old den. The mouse has chalked a rule of its own: RULE ONE. RUN.
items.line: {glee}That's the best rule I've heard.

items.name: jar
items.text: A jar of glow on a post, half-sunk in the leaf-litter. The mist makes it a green moon.
items.line: {awed}It's a moon. It's a tiny moon on a stick.

items.name: rule7
items.text: RULE SEVEN. DON'T ANSWER IT. And below, in a different hand, a shaky addition: (IT SOUNDS LIKE ANYONE YOU KNOW.)
items.line: {scared}...Don't answer it. I won't. I'm not going to. ...Who?

items.name: bell
items.text: A bell in a trap-frame, the cord sprung and the felt still on. It was a warning bell. It was wrapped so it couldn't be a warning.
items.line: {worried}They set a trap that couldn't ring. ...That's not a trap. That's a hope.

items.name: shoes
items.text: A rack of shoes with every sole felted, and a space on the rail the size of one pair. Somebody went out in a hurry in their good shoes.
items.line: {sad}Not the good ones. Never go out in the good ones.

items.name: thorn
items.text: A thorn tree with a white rag tied on every branch, all of them tied by the same hand. Somebody came alone, and wished many times.
items.line: {sad}That's a lot of wishing for one person.

items.name: rule6
items.text: RULE SIX. DON'T LOOK UP. The sign has been put up very low, so you won't have to.
items.line: {worried}I'm not looking up. I'm looking at the sign. It's a nice sign.

items.name: giant
items.text: A great trunk across the maze's mouth, and the other trunks have gone round it, as water goes round a stone. In the wood, even a fallen thing has the right of way.
items.line: {awed}Everything's polite here. Even the trees.

items.name: shrine
items.text: A shrine at a corner of the walls: a felted candle, a clay bird, a thimble that held water once. It's long dry.
items.line: {thinking}Nobody's topped it up. That's fine. That's allowed.

items.name: jar
items.text: A jar of glow set where two walls meet, so you'd know the corner was a corner. It's the only way to tell, in the mist.
items.line: {proud}A corner light! That's what I'd do.

items.name: rule
items.text: A rule on a board by the water: LET THE RIVER BE LOUD. The mill-folk's one exception, scratched in after the rest. The river was the only thing allowed to speak.
items.line: {glee}The river gets to talk! Lucky river.

items.name: thorn
items.text: A thorn tree at the water's edge with cloth strips tied in the river-side branches. The mill-folk's wishes: for rain, for wheel-grease, for a quiet winter.
items.line: {thinking}A quiet winter. They got one, didn't they.

items.name: jar
items.text: A jar of glow on a mooring post at the race. The water takes the light and gives back a greener one.
items.line: {awed}It's green on the water too! Look! Two jars!

items.name: bell
items.text: The mill bell, wrapped in felt. A mill with no bell to say the hour ends: the folk worked by the sun and the stomach.
items.line: {sheepish}My stomach would have been a good bell.

items.name: rule8
items.text: RULE EIGHT. A board with the rule painted over, white, and then written on again in the white: THERE IS NO RULE EIGHT. (WE RAN OUT OF TIME.)
items.line: {scared}...They ran out of rules. Sword, they ran out of rules.

items.name: shrine
items.text: A shrine on the edge of the Quiet: the candle stub is the biggest you've seen. It's never been lit. A stone beside it is warm from the sun, and your hand wants to stay on it.
items.line: {sad}It's warm. Why's the rock warm? It's the Quiet.

items.name: thorn
items.text: A thorn tree at the Quiet's edge, with no cloth on it at all. Only the knots, left behind, where the strips were pulled off all at once.
items.line: {scared}Something took them. ...Or someone took them down. In a hurry.

items.name: jar
items.text: A jar of glow, the last on the path, its moss going pale from the cold. You're not sure it's meant to light anything now. It just marks where the lights stop.
items.line: {worried}That's where the lights stop. ...Don't go further. ...Go further.

items.name: bell
items.text: A bell on a post at the bridge's end, felt-wrapped, with a second wrap over the first and a third over that. It's been wrapped more than anything you've seen.
items.line: {scared}They really, really, really didn't want it to ring.

items.name: sign
items.text: A board at the bridge's end: CROSS ONE AT A TIME. DON'T LOOK DOWN. DON'T LOOK BACK. It runs out of board before it runs out of advice.
items.line: {worried}That's a lot of don'ts for a bridge.

items.name: shoes
items.text: A rack of felt shoes before the bridge, the last pairs in the wood. Somebody's lined them up toe to heel. Some of them are very small.
items.line: {sad}...They changed their shoes for the bridge. Of course they did.

items.name: thorn
items.text: A thorn bush by the bridge-foot, hung with a last wish or two. The newest strip is the colour of your sleeve. You check. It isn't yours.
items.line: {sly}Is it yours? It looks like yours.

items.name: jar
items.text: A jar of glow on a hook screwed into a root, the only light but yours. In the dark under the wood, somebody thought of a night-light.
items.line: {awed}It's a night-light. Somebody put a night-light down here.

items.name: jar2
items.text: A second jar, further on, hung low. The glow is dimmer. It's the spare, in case the first one fails, in case anybody would need it.
items.line: {proud}Two! They thought of two!

items.name: shrine
items.text: A shrine in a hollow of a root: a felted candle and a child's drawing of the sky, so the dark can know what it's missing.
items.line: {sad}That's for the dark. That's so nice.

items.name: stump
items.text: A root-house with a round door and a window lit green with glow-moss. Tiny curtains. Somebody's put out a doormat the size of a button.
items.line: {glee}Somebody lives down here!

items.name: bed
items.text: A bedroll, still rolled the way a careful person rolls one. The pack beside it has a tin mug and half a biscuit, and the biscuit has been half-eaten for fifty years. Somebody camped at the gate to be first through.
items.line: {thoughtful}First through. I'd rather be second. Second gets to see what happens to first.

items.name: sticks
items.text: A barrel of walking sticks, and one hat on top. Left at the gate by people who thought they wouldn't need them. Every stick has a name burned into it. Most are worn off.
items.line: {bored}A coat-stand for people who thought they were done walking. Optimistic.

items.name: queue
items.text: Two brass posts and a red rope. A queue, for a gate. Somebody thought the Hero would be popular.
items.line: {laughing}There's no queue. There's us. ...Do we form one?

items.name: chair
items.text: A chair set at an angle facing the gate, so someone could watch for the hero in comfort. The seat is worn pale. Chairs don't go that pale in a year.
items.line: {sad}Somebody watched a long time. That's a lot of looking at a door.

items.name: kettle
items.text: A ring of fire-stones and a black kettle, the ash crusted over. The lid is still on.
items.line: {smile}Tea at the end of the world. I respect that.

items.name: fountain
items.text: A round fountain, dry as a bone. A plinth stands in the middle with nothing on top. The water used to come from the statue's hands. Moss has filled the basin, and a single brass coin is left in it.
items.line: {thoughtful}Dry. A fountain's the first thing to go. You don't notice one until the sound stops.

items.name: feet
items.text: A plinth with only the boots left on it: stone boots, toes up, a little cracked, standing as if the rest of the person had stepped out. Which may be exactly what happened.
items.line: {laughing}Out of the boots and gone. I've felt the urge.

items.name: banner
items.text: A banner on a pole, faded to pink. Four poles ring this court. Three have banners. The fourth has a pair of socks, which somebody had the sense to hang out.
items.line: {smile}Practical.

items.name: stall
items.text: A stall at the court's edge, striped awning faded to pale blue. A chalk card on the counter: LAST DAY. EVERYTHING MUST GO. Everything did.
items.line: {bored}Everything must go. Spot on.

items.name: laundry
items.text: A laundry slab, scrubbed hollow by years of wrists, with a violet bar of soap still sitting in the dip, shrunk to a pebble.
items.line: {smile}Violet. Fancy. Even the washing was fancy.

items.name: bell
items.text: A bell on a post by a door, wrapped in felt and tied with string. Even here. Even in the city, where nobody walks, they wrapped the bell.
items.line: {worried}Even here. They knew it was coming. ...They knew a long time.

items.name: shoes
items.text: Soft shoes on a rack by the last gate, felt-soled, in every size, set out as if for a long line. For the last stretch, you changed your shoes.
items.line: {thoughtful}A shoe stand at the edge of the world. That's very polite.

items.name: stall
items.text: A stall with its shutter down and a card: CLOSED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE. THANK YOU FOR YOUR PATIENCE. The card has been left to curl at the corners.
items.line: {bored}Further notice. We're all waiting on that.

items.name: banner
items.text: A banner on a pole, torn to ribbons and pink as a shell. Under the faded gold: the city's motto, in small letters: WE ARE LISTENING.
items.line: {worried}We are listening. ...To what?

items.name: tower
items.text: A tower of books that has leaned, in fifty years, about a thumb's width. A slip of paper marks the place: PAGE 40 OF 41. The last page isn't in the book. You check.
items.line: {bored}Page forty of forty-one. And forty-one isn't there. Of course not.

items.name: globe
items.text: A globe. The seas have faded to the same tan as the land, so the world is one dusty ball with writing on it. There's a pin in a place that isn't on any map you know.
items.line: {thoughtful}A pin. Somebody knew where they were going. That's more than I can say.

items.name: sheet
items.text: Something under a dust sheet, shaped like a desk with an opinion. You lift a corner: a desk. You lower it. It's the sort of room that makes you whisper.
items.line: {shy}Why am I whispering?

items.name: tower2
items.text: A second tower, this one fallen over and put back together wrong, with the spines facing in. A note on top: SORT LATER.
items.line: {bored}Later. The great tradition.

items.name: slab
items.text: A washing slab at the water's edge, scrubbed hollow by years of wrists. A bar of soap sits in the dip, shrunk to a violet pebble.
items.line: {smile}Fancy soap. Even the laundry had standards.

items.name: cattail
items.text: Cattails, thick as a fence at the pool's lip. They've climbed the aqueduct's stone and think they own it.
items.line: {bored}They'd win an election, honestly.

items.name: steps
items.text: Stepping stones across the shallows, laid so no one would ever wet their feet. They've sunk a little. You'll wet your feet.
items.line: {smile}Excellent planning. For a different century.

items.name: boot
items.text: A single boot at the pool's edge, half-sunk, a frog sitting in it like it's the only chair in town.
items.line: {laughing}It's got a tenant. Don't evict it.

items.name: stall1
items.text: A stall between two pillars, awning faded to pale stripes. The scales are still on the counter, one pan up, one down: weighing something when it stopped. A mouse has moved into the empty pan.
items.line: {laughing}Two ounces of mouse. Fair price.

items.name: stall2
items.text: A stall with a hand-lettered card: BACK IN FIVE MINUTES. The ink says it was written with a very steady hand, which is how you write a polite lie.
items.line: {bored}Five minutes. Excellent timekeeping.

items.name: banner
items.text: A banner at the colonnade's end, torn, one corner hanging. The picture on it was a lantern. The lantern has faded the least.
items.line: {thoughtful}The lantern outlasted the rest. Lanterns do that.

items.name: bed
items.text: A bedroll tucked behind a pillar, the blanket folded square. A tag on the strap: PLEASE DON'T MOVE. Whoever it was, they planned to be back.
items.line: {sad}Don't move it. I won't.

items.name: globe
items.text: A reading-room globe with a brass ring round it, tilted to the angle of somebody leaning to see. There's a thumbprint at the north.
items.line: {thoughtful}They checked the north. Everyone checks the north.

items.name: tower
items.text: A book tower by the armchair, three open at once, face down: somebody reading three things at the same time. The tower is the height of a bored person's patience.
items.line: {bored}Three at once. I do that. It means none of them are good.

items.name: sheet
items.text: A sheet over a reading-lamp and a footstool, shaped like a patient animal.
items.line: {shy}It's waiting for somebody to come back and read. It's very patient.

items.name: ticket
items.text: A ticket post by the door: TAKE A NUMBER. QUIET PLEASE. The roll holds one ticket, and it's 0001.
items.line: {laughing}Number one. Not first. Just number one.

items.name: statue
items.text: A figure half-freed from its block: shoulders, a chin, the idea of a face. The chisel marks stop mid-line, as if the sculptor was called to dinner. A mallet waits on one shoulder.
items.line: {bored}He got as far as the chin. The chin is excellent.

items.name: feet
items.text: A plinth waiting for a finished statue, and on it a pair of stone boots: the first bit done. Somebody always starts at the bottom.
items.line: {thoughtful}Start at the feet. Good advice for most things.

items.name: sheet
items.text: A sheet over a statue, and the statue's outline looks like a person holding up a lantern. You don't lift the sheet.
items.line: {worried}Leave it. I mean it. Leave it.

items.name: slab
items.text: A grinding slab for pigment: red, ochre, a lump of blue the size of an egg. The blue is still bright. Everything else faded around it.
items.line: {smile}Fifty years and the blue is still the best part.

items.name: sheet
items.text: A big dust sheet over a table with four chairs, as if the meeting broke up in a hurry and somebody was tidy about it.
items.line: {bored}Meeting adjourned. Permanently.

items.name: tower
items.text: A tower of ledgers by the crack, each labelled with a year. The newest is open on top: the page is blank, except one line. A date. And: SEE NEXT.
items.line: {thoughtful}See next. There isn't a next. ...Is there?

items.name: cart
items.text: A file cart parked half in the crack, its boxes ready to go. One box says OUTGOING. One says INCOMING. The third says WHATEVER THAT IS.
items.line: {laughing}I like the third box.

items.name: queue
items.text: Queue posts leading to the crack in the wall, a sign hanging from the rope: THIS WAY FOR APPEALS.
items.line: {bored}Appeals. To what? The wall?

items.name: cart
items.text: A cart of file boxes in the cellar, each lid taped shut with a red seal. The seals are unbroken. Nothing in here was ever meant to be looked at.
items.line: {worried}Don't break the seals. Don't. ...I'm tempted. Don't let me.

items.name: sheet
items.text: A dust sheet over a heap that rises in the middle, then falls: a desk, a lamp, a very tall plant that never got watered.
items.line: {bored}Tall plant. Poor plant.

items.name: tower
items.text: A tower of damp ledgers, swollen to twice their size. The top one has a note on it: WE'LL DRY THESE. A second note, later: WE WILL DRY THESE.
items.line: {smile}Optimism in two handwritings.

items.name: globe
items.text: A globe in the cellar, face to the wall. Somebody turned it round and didn't want to look at it.
items.line: {thoughtful}Somebody didn't want to see the world. I understand them a little.

items.name: cart
items.text: A cart of counting-boards stacked like loaves. The topmost board has a tally with a thumb-sized hole poked through the sixth mark.
items.line: {bored}They got bored at six. I'd have got bored at three.

items.name: ticket
items.text: A ticket post by the counting desks. The roll has run out, but one ticket is stuck in the slot: 0000. A note: DON'T.
items.line: {shy}Zero. Not even one. Not even a start.

items.name: globe
items.text: A globe at the desk's end, spun last by an impatient hand: it's stopped with a hole where the pin was.
items.line: {thoughtful}Somebody pulled the pin out. Just left. As a gesture.

items.name: sheet
items.text: A big dust sheet over something four-legged. It's a stool. You are sure it's a stool.
items.line: {shy}It's a stool. Don't lift it.

items.name: tower
items.text: A tower of books in the stacks' aisle, one stack tall, one stack wide. A sticky note on it: PLEASE RESHELVE. A second, below: IT IS REALLY VERY HIGH UP.
items.line: {bored}Please reshelve. Please reach.

items.name: cart
items.text: A file cart on its side by the shelves, its books spilled in a fan. A fallen ladder beside it. Somebody went for a high book and the cart had other ideas.
items.line: {laughing}High shelf wins again.

items.name: globe
items.text: A globe at the end of the aisle, parked in the dust. Someone has drawn a small line on it from this room to a place you can't read. A trip planned and not taken.
items.line: {thoughtful}A trip they never took. We've all got one.

items.name: sheet
items.text: A sheet over a tall shape at the aisle's far end: a clerk's high stool, or a ghost with good posture.
items.line: {shy}Ghost with good posture. That's my guess.

items.name: queue
items.text: Two queue posts and a rope, and the carpet worn into a track where hundreds of people stood and shuffled and stood. The track goes round the room twice and ends at a desk with a CLOSED sign.
items.line: {bored}They queued for years. To be told to ask again tomorrow.

items.name: ticket
items.text: A dispenser with a roll of paper numbers. You tear one off: 0001. Nothing happens. You hold it for a bit, in case.
items.line: {bored}Number one. Not first in line. Just number one. It's different.

items.name: sheet
items.text: A bench under a dust sheet, shaped like a long, flat, slightly disappointed animal.
items.line: {smile}A sheeted bench. Somebody tidied the waiting. It's the saddest thing I've seen all day.

items.name: cart
items.text: A trolley of forms: FORM 1. FORM 1A. FORM 1A (REVISED). The top form asks for your name, your age, and a reason. The reason has a very small box.
items.line: {laughing}Reason: small box.

items.name: feast
items.text: A trestle table laid for a feast: forty plates, forty cups, a cake the size of a cartwheel gone to green velvet. Among the plates, a card in a careful hand: FOR THE HERO. WHEN HE COMES. (START WITHOUT HIM IF IT GETS LATE.)
items.line: {sad}They put out all the good plates. ...Nobody started. Look, nobody started.

items.name: bunting1
items.text: Bunting strung between two posts, the flags faded to the colours of weak tea. One's lost a corner, and the string still holds the shape of the wind that used to blow.
items.line: {awed}They hung flags. For the Hero. ...For whoever.

items.name: bunting2
items.text: A second string of bunting, further down the square, hung to meet the first. Somebody's measured it, and it doesn't quite. Two flags short, and then a ribbon.
items.line: {thinking}They ran out of flags. They tied a ribbon. Good thinking.

items.name: flowers
items.text: Wild flowers coming up through the cobbles in a line, as if the stones had been laid with a gap for them. Some days a town can't help having a garden.
items.line: {grin}They came up in a row! They're organised!

items.name: mouse
items.text: A mouse has made a house in an upturned bucket by the well, with a door cut in the side and a doormat made of a leaf.
items.line: {glee}A mouse in a bucket. That's so smart.

items.name: jar
items.text: A jar of glow-moss on a post by the well-bottom landing. Somebody lowered it down on a rope and left it, in case anyone fell, or anyone came down to find them.
items.line: {worried}A light for whoever fell. ...That's what I'd do.

items.name: tally
items.text: A chalk tally on the wall, six marks, then a seventh crossing them, and a seventh again, as if someone gave up counting days and began counting something else.
items.line: {sad}It stops counting days. It starts counting... what?

items.name: face
items.text: A chalk face on the wall with a big smile and an arrow pointing UP. Underneath, a child's writing: THIS WAY OUT. (WE THINK.)
items.line: {proud}That's the right way. I can read upside down.

items.name: moss
items.text: A patch of moss on the old stones, fat and green in the dark, as if something down here cares about the damp.
items.line: {thinking}It likes it here. Good for it.

items.name: sheet
items.text: A dust sheet over a stack of crates, the corner chewed. A tiny nest is built in the folds: three mice and a toast crust.
items.line: {glee}They've got a whole flat!

items.name: flags
items.text: A bundle of spare flags, rolled tight, tied with string: WELCOME (SPARE). They never took them out. You leave them rolled.
items.line: {sad}Spare welcome. They kept a spare.

items.name: cart
items.text: A stores trolley of tinned goods and paper-wrapped parcels, labelled: HERO'S SUPPER (HOT). The parcels are very cold.
items.line: {worried}Hero's supper. Nobody ate it. Nobody ate it, Sword.

items.name: bunting
items.text: Bunting strung from the mill's gable to a post in the yard, the flags faded to pastel. MILL OPEN DAY, says a board beneath. The date has run.
items.line: {awed}An open day! Open to everyone! Even us!

items.name: flowers
items.text: A tuft of wild flowers growing from a crack in the millstone's old plinth. Yellow, pink, white. The only thing in the mill still turning to the sun.
items.line: {grin}Flowers! On a rock! That's brave!

items.name: barrow
items.text: A wheelbarrow tipped on its side with a note chalked on the underside: GONE FOR HELP. BACK SOON.
items.line: {sad}Back soon. ...Does it say how soon?

items.name: sacks
items.text: A pile of flour sacks, one slit and spilled into a fan. A line of mouse prints crosses it, and returns, and crosses again. A busy road.
items.line: {glee}A mouse highway!

items.name: stump
items.text: A mill-stump with a tiny door and a tin-lid roof. A thread of smoke would be rising if it weren't unlit.
items.line: {sly}Is it a house? A tiny house?

items.name: flowers
items.text: Wild flowers in a doorstep crack. They've got every colour a doorstep can have.
items.line: {grin}Somebody's garden's still going.

items.name: mouse
items.text: A mouse's door at the foot of a garden wall, a pea-pod for a doorbell. It's pulled shut, tightly.
items.line: {glee}Doorbell! Doorbell! No, don't.

items.name: bunting
items.text: A short string of bunting between two garden posts, as welcome as it was fifty years ago, which is to say very, very faded.
items.line: {awed}Even the gardens put out flags.

items.name: shoes
items.text: A rack of felt shoes outside a garden gate, set out, in rows, for a long line of visitors. Not one pair's been moved.
items.line: {sad}Not one pair's been touched. They were all waiting for somebody to need them.
